title: Conjectural coefficient pattern for Gaussian integer polynomials
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and set $r=(p-1)^2$. Define

$$
g_p(x)=\prod_{\substack{1\leq n,m\leq p-1\\(p,n^2+m^2)=1}}(x-(n+mi))=x^{(p-1)^2}+a_1x^{(p-1)^2-1}+\cdots+a_{r-1}x+a_r.
$$

**Conjectural coefficient pattern.** If $p=4k+3>3$, then

$$
g_p(x)\equiv 1+x^{2(p-1)}+x^{4(p-1)}+\cdots+x^{(p-1)^2}\equiv\frac{1-x^{p^2-1}}{1-x^{2(p-1)}}\pmod p.
$$

If $p=4k+1>5$, then

$$
g_p(x)\equiv 1+b_1x^{p-1}+b_2x^{2(p-1)}+\cdots+x^{(p-1)(p-3)}\pmod p,
$$

where $b_j\equiv a_{j(p-1)}\pmod p$. The displayed pattern is based on computations; the source asks whether a closed formula for the coefficients $b_j$ exists.
references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2203.03942](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.03942), [arXiv:1502.02423](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.02423), [arXiv:1308.5392](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.5392).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07978

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).
source_name: Nikita Kalinin, “Wolstenholme's theorem over Gaussian integers”, arXiv:2504.07978 (2025).
